title: Writing Weights or Training Them? Spatial Reasoning through Weight-Space Programming and Low-Rank Adaptation
why_wsp: Evaluates the public WSP patch p50c (LLM-written edit to two Qwen3.5-0.8B MLP down-projections) on spatial reasoning, attempts further gradient-free edits (one by GPT-6 Astra with weight/activation tool access, others designed from mechanistic measurements), and compares against LoRA.
domain: LLM text-based spatial reasoning (reference-frame task, StepGame) with distance-comparison off-target tasks
editor: p50c from original WSP work (editor not re-run here); GPT-6 Astra for one further edit; remaining edits designed by the authors from probes
interface: code/tensor tools (Astra given tool access to weights and activations); closed form for author-designed edits
loop: one-shot for evaluated patch; editing sessions used a development subset with pre-set gates
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: p50c: 'differs from the base model in exactly two tensors, the MLP down-projections of layers 15 and 19 (7,340,032 elements, of which 130,188 differ after BF16 storage)' (Sec. 3.1); Table 2 lists 0.016%. Astra edit: '85,519 BF16 values, 0.011% of the weights' (Sec. 4)

headline_results.claim: p50c gains on target tasks (thinking on, 3 seeds)
headline_results.quote: the public patch (p50c) raised mean accuracy from 0.0% to 22.1% on the reference-frame task and from 19.2% to 33.7% on StepGame
Two independent permutations scored 1/128 and 3/128 on the reference frame and 39/200 and 40/200 on StepGame, the same as the base model
126 to 127 of its 128 reference-frame outputs and 135 to 140 of its 200 StepGame outputs reached the 32,768-token limit, whereas p50c reached it on 3 and 5

headline_results.claim: Astra's further edit no better than random perturbation
headline_results.quote: On the full benchmark this edit scored 31/128 and 65/200, below the seed-matched p50c scores of 34/128 and 69/200 and indistinguishable from a matched random perturbation (26/128 and 67/200).

headline_results.claim: LoRA collapses off-target distance tasks; p50c preserves them
headline_results.quote: p50c answered 120.3/128 and 118.0/128 correctly on average, whereas all three adapters scored between 0 and 2 on both families

baselines_and_controls: base model; element-permuted p50c delta (same norm/sparsity); matched random perturbation for Astra edit; prompting with method description and worked examples; thinking-off with visible reasoning; LoRA rank 1 and 16 (answer-only vs worked-solution supervision, from base vs from p50c); off-target distance tasks; held-out templates/levels/cells
runs_and_variance: three sampling seeds for main comparisons (e.g. p50c 34/25/26 on reference frame); editing and control evaluations single-seed; 'Each adapter was trained once, so the three evaluation seeds measure sampling variation rather than training variation.' (Sec. 10)
robustness_of_edits: Off-target preservation tested: p50c keeps >90% on distance tasks; robustness to fine-tuning/quantization not tested
verification: statistical (exact McNemar tests, pre-registered improvement criterion Eq. 2, hash-verified items and prompts)
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a for editor; analysis shows p50c restores termination of an existing computation rather than adding spatial skill; linear probes for |dx| vs |dy| near chance (0.536), so no signal for closed-form write to amplify.
limitations_stated: One 0.8B model and 2D tasks; adapters trained once; editing and LoRA used different data and compute budgets; unsuccessful edits do not rule out other editing strategies; probe failures do not prove absence of computation; benchmark items inspected before experiments; off-target evaluation limited to two families.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 'Sparks of weight-space programming' (p50c patch, Qwen3.5-0.8B MATH-500 7.9% to 48.1%)
notes_for_survey: Controlled head-to-head of a published WSP edit vs LoRA on one backbone. The WSP patch's gain depends on edit structure (permuted delta does nothing) and acts by stopping looping, while preserving neighbouring skills; LoRA reaches ceiling but hijacks off-target tasks. An Astra-written follow-up edit was indistinguishable from random perturbation.
